decisions.reason: As a niche hardware item with limited visible traction after launch, Product D is more likely to have fallen below aspiration levels, and this firm has shown it will reallocate such resources to stronger core and development activities.

Product E remains close to the firm's core control-systems business for water infrastructure, so even with uncertain recent evidence management would likely tolerate short-term ambiguity and keep it while results are judged against strategic aspirations.

Because Product F fits the firm's shift toward connected, software-based and data-driven infrastructure management, available organizational slack and its strong relatedness to existing capabilities support keeping it unless clearer underperformance appears.
